scope: Keep a malformed but size-delimited OBJECTS record local to its object-map frame, while retaining strict refusal and integrity-sensitive partial-output refusal.

basis.odaSpecification: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1, §20.1 (common non-entity object format) and §23.1–23.2 (per-object map locations).
basis.principle: The outer object size and object-map location bound each object independently. A corrupt common prologue makes that object unpublishable but does not move the next object's location.

implementation.change: When the frame is readable but the common prologue or common handle tail is invalid, record an ObjectFrameBounds integrity error and return a record failure without setting the OBJECTS section structural-failure flag. The frame ledger marks the object Failed; later object-map frames continue to be read.

generatedMalformedFrame.origin: Locally authored in a temporary directory for this test; not committed as a fixture.
generatedMalformedFrame.shape: One custom-class OBJECTS frame retains an encoded object type and handle but truncates before common EED/reactor state; a valid LINE follows.

controls: For AC1021, AC1024, and AC1032, ASCII and Binary strict conversion refuse and preserve a destination sentinel.

The same explicit-partial ASCII and Binary requests emit the incomplete-output warning but still refuse because the retained integrity ledger contains an ObjectFrameBounds error; destination and source bytes remain unchanged.
Direct DWG callback observation proves the valid LINE after the bad object remains readable and frame accounting is exact.

results: PASS: 48 partial-read strict/partial/readback controls, including the malformed OBJECTS matrix
PASS: 48 skipped-record and raw-only controls after the reader disposition change

limits: The malformed body is a synthetic negative control, not evidence for producer-authored object schemas or successful lossy export.
AC1027 is excluded because the generated profile hits an independent source-reference closure error before isolated CLI output disposition.
